signal: Caterpillar is down 34% in 3 months (-49% from its 2026-06-30 high) while sales, operating profit and cash flow all grew year over year.

evidence.fact: Q3 2026 sales $20.7B vs $17.6B (+17%); operating profit margin 20.4% vs 17.3%; record backlog stated in the release.
XBRL discrete quarters: operating income $4,214M vs $3,052M (+38%); operating cash flow $4,352M vs $3,737M; capex $697M vs $658M; free cash flow up 19%.

so_what: A heavy-equipment maker with record backlog is priced as if orders will fall. Either the market sees a cycle peak or an AI/data-center power trade unwinding; the filings show neither yet.
ask_next: What is the stated backlog and order trend in the 10-Q, how much of the 2026 run-up (about 570 to 1,060) was a power-generation/AI-capex theme, and does Deere (DE, +22% 6m) tell a different story?

signal: Datadog is down 30% in 3 months after a quarter with 35% revenue growth, its first sizeable GAAP operating profit and rising cash flow.

evidence.fact: Q3 2026 revenue $1.20B (+35%); GAAP operating income $75M vs -$6M a year ago; operating cash flow $290M, free cash flow $251M.
XBRL discrete quarters: operating cash flow $290M vs $251M, capex $11M vs $17M.

so_what: Software was sold as a group (see INTU, NOW, ADBE) on seat-compression fears. Datadog is usage-priced, not seat-priced, so the fear fits it poorly. The market may not be separating the two.
ask_next: Is Datadog revenue priced per host/usage (not per seat) per the 10-K, and what did the stock do in the 3 days after 2026-11-04?

signal: Intuit is down 21% in 3 months and 59% from its Dec 2025 high even though revenue, operating income and cash flow keep growing and the quarter beat guidance.

evidence.fact: Q1 FY27 (Oct quarter) revenue +12% to $4.4B, above top of guidance; agreement to sell Mailchimp (revenue -1%) to Bending Spoons.
XBRL: operating income $868M vs $534M (+63%); operating cash flow $1,062M vs $637M; capex $75M vs $38M.

so_what: Tax and small-business accounting software priced for AI disruption while the filings show growth. Watch for whether the market fear is about consumer tax filing being displaced by AI agents.
ask_next: Read the 10-Q risk factors and the Q1 call-free release text for any consumer TurboTax unit or customer-count decline; is the 59% fall from the high a multiple reset only?

signal: Nvidia fell from 214 to 149 (about -30%) around a quarter with revenue +103% because its founder-CEO resigned on 2026-11-11 and was reinstated on 2026-11-22.

evidence.fact: Q3 FY27 revenue $115.8B (+103% YoY, +20% QoQ); operating income $77.5B vs $36.0B; $28.1B returned to holders; buyback authority up $150B.
8-K Item 5.02: CEO resigned 2026-11-11, CFO Kress interim; board reinstated the founder CEO 2026-11-22.

so_what: Price is fighting a clearly strong quarter, but there is a named governance shock, so this is not 'nobody cares'. Fundamentals XBRL (10-Q for the October quarter) is not filed yet; the facts here are from the release.
ask_next: Why did the CEO resign and return (read the full 8-K and any 8-K/A), and does the October-quarter 10-Q show anything the release did not?

signal: FIS is down 31% in 3 months to 27.6 (-58% from its January high), but the fundamentals gap is smaller than the headline: 27% revenue growth is mostly an acquisition; organic (pro forma) growth is 3.7%.

evidence.fact: Q3 2026 GAAP revenue +27% to $3.5B but pro forma revenue +3.7%; adjusted EPS +6.6%; free cash flow $862M (+8%); 2026 free cash flow guide $2.15-2.25B.
XBRL: operating income $660M vs $457M; operating cash flow up about 24%.

so_what: A bank-processing rail that is cash generative but whose reported growth is bought, not organic. The price drop may be about debt/deal risk, which the headline XBRL numbers hide.
ask_next: From the 10-Q balance sheet and debt note, what is net debt and interest cost after the acquisition, and what drives organic growth near 3-4%?

signal: Capital-markets and card banks are being sold while their earnings rise; regional/consumer banks are up. GS, MS, SCHW, COF, BAC all fell 14-23% in 3 months with improving operating results.

evidence.fact: 3m price change: GS -23%, MS -21%, BAC -22%, COF -16%, SCHW -14%; 6m: GS -19%, MS -16% vs WFC +8%, USB +9%, PNC +2%.
GS pre-tax earnings $7,003M vs $5,392M (+30%) in the September quarter; quarterly cash-flow figures are noisy for banks and not used.
MS 10-Q for the September quarter; pre-tax +7% YoY on revenue +5%.

so_what: Not a uniform bank sell-off. The split could be a rate-path or trading-revenue peak worry, but the filings show no earnings deterioration yet. JPM and C XBRL were stale or sparse in this screen, so not scored.
ask_next: Break down GS/MS/BAC revenue by trading vs fee vs net interest income; which line is the market discounting? Pull JPM and C separately.

signal: WARNING (reverse): homebuilders PHM, TOL and DHI are up 7-14% over 6 months while their revenue is falling 3-10% and operating profit is down; GPN is up 32% over 6 months while operating profit fell.

evidence.fact: 6m price: PHM +14%, TOL +11%, DHI +7%, GPN +32%.
PHM revenue -10% YoY in each of the last two quarters; free cash flow down 33% in the September quarter.
TOL revenue -10%, operating income -26% (July quarter); DHI revenue -3%, operating income -16%.
GPN revenue +64% (acquisition) but operating income -68% and free cash flow negative in the September quarter.

so_what: Price is ahead of weak numbers. For homebuilders this may be a bet on the rate turn (the Berkshire view) rather than current results; the Taylor Morrison deal may also be lifting peers (unverified). Do not treat the bounce as proof of recovery.
ask_next: What are the net new orders, backlog and gross margin trend in the PHM/TOL/DHI filings, and what did mortgage rates do over the same window?
